1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.

Hi. Your problem is that you play reactively instead of proactively. Your team is uncoordinated and you either win the round by killing 3 or watch your whole team die because you all went in without a plan. Your aim is good and your gunfight intuition is solid but you fail to put yourself in good positions and are forced to try and deal with whatever randomly happens in the round. Here's what to do instead: On attack, you need to be calling plays for your team. They can be simple (e.g. what you did on round 6 was good), but you almost never do this. It's not even about reading the enemy, it's about looking at what utility your team has and putting forward a barebones plan for how the round is going to go. "Gekko, flash our Raze into shower, she can take the space with her satchels. Reyna, come blind out short with me after I smoke." or "Cypher trip the shower push and sit A short, we're gonna make noise hookah and you can kill them if they try to TP." Honestly, from my perspective, it's a miracle you guys even won 5 rounds with no plan. Even in low immortal I've seen teams of 5 perfectly competent players run it down 5-man A short and lose because nobody called a shower split. You cannot play the game like this. Also, I see a lot of people do the smoke on A that cuts from dice to showers, and I don't understand why. I think this is a terrible smoke and you should almost never do this. Yeah I had in mind this thing that Hooj says about intuition when I typed the review. I've a piece of advice in this regard actually, something that worked wonders with me and I hope it can help you too: It's basically limit-testing. Make arbitrary decisions all the time, even about minor things, and stick to them (unless it's immediately obvious that it's going to end badly, for instance if you go for a play and you can hear the entire enemy team running your way, you probably should turn back lol). Like, "I am going to fight here, really make a stand" ; "I am going to take this orb" ; "I'm going to push for flank early." Those are the kind that can be established pre-round, and preferably communicated to the team so that they can help, but do some mid-round too. Like, you end up in a man-disadvantage: "I am going to sneak push this specific area until I find a pick (even though I could end up not finding anyone at all)" ; "We have absolutely no idea about any of the enemies positions, I need to look for info, so I'm going to burn a flash around this corner for a quick peek (even though my agent sucks at gathering info, there could be no-one at all and I'll have 'wasted' a flash)". Or in the post-plant: "I'm going to set myself up here and look for the enemy coming this specific way (even though there might be 3 or 4 other paths that the enemies could be coming from)." 1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.

Or in the post-plant: "I'm going to set myself up here and look for the enemy coming this specific way (even though there might be 3 or 4 other paths that the enemies could be coming from)." 19:18 So I'm not going to say that this was a necessarily bad play, but the reason why pros do this play with neon is because she can stun the smoke alongside the breach stun. Otherwise, as you can see, they just run through and take the fight. With raze here I don't think it's optimal. In this case, since its planted in the corner, they could only be defusing from the right. Therefore, you should be directing most of your bullets slightly right of the ping.  Overall, you should just be more aware of what your team is doing and where they are: play with them or, if you're playing to keep map control, jiggle/jump peek, and if their pushing try to fall back and play with your team, or, as raze, nade to isolate and then take your 1.

1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.

1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.

I watched your VOD and overall there isn’t too much to criticize, but there are a few areas you can improve. Your peeking is a bit weak and sometimes you could be more confident when taking space. For example in A Main when Breach stunned you had the chance to prime dash and push through. It wasn’t a huge mistake to hold back, but those are the kinds of plays that can open rounds. Your ability usage is fine, though I noticed you throw a lot of panic smokes. That’s not the end of the world, but I did notice you don’t use your smokes much to help your team. A clear example was Round 7 where you could have smoked for Sova so he could defuse safely. Right now your gameplay leans a little selfish, which helps your KD but will hurt your team’s chances of winning rounds. Your economy could also use some work. Buying a Sheriff second round is risky since it usually forces you into a weaker buy on the enemy bonus. Sometimes a Sheriff can win an eco, but it is not very consistent. Since you are playing Jett, I think you should practice with the Outlaw and make it part of your second round or half-buy options because it gives you a lot more value. Finally, your minimap awareness is inconsistent. In Round 16 Brim rotated and you and phoenix sat on your thumbs for a tad too long  as much as brim shouldnt have rotated you need to be aware of the spikes location...

Nice game and performance. I noticed a few things you should try to work on: Remember that you are playing Omen, not Jett or Reyna. If you're going to play aggressively, try to have a teammate that can provide utility for your play. Otherwise you may get punished, especially in higher ranks. Don't snap reload after one or two shots, it's not a good habit and can cost you rounds. Don't put smokes that block teammate vision. I get that it protects you from angles, but enemies can swing out of smokes nevertheless and catch a timing. Also they can play within smokes, and this is very hard to clear for you. Don't rely on your utility too much in combat. Omen's utility is great, but when enemies are close to you it is better to just take the 1v1 and not get caught with your utility out. In low numbers (e.g. 2v2, 2v1 etc.) try to play with your teammate so that you can trade them out if they die, otherwise, there's a risk that the 2v2 becomes a 1v2 which is much harder to convert.

1. **No insta-crouching.** Great control of shots with secondary, but ensure that there is no crouching from long rangle with a phantom/vandal.
  2. **Effectiveness of play.** We need to make sure we are not wasting time or wasting bullets when playing around the map. Be faster on your rotates and pushes, no need to hang back, you should be going in second/third after your duelist.

  4. **Fight with your team more.** You could be a bit more aware of your teammates and their positioning. Try to fight with them, instead of peeking afterwards. Trading is great, but if both of you stay alive, that's even better.

1. You overpeek way too much. If valorant was about getting from your spawn as far into enemy territory as possible in the shortest amount of time you would be Radiant, but unfortunately it’s not. After you clear the site and plant your job is to STALL as long as possible so the enemies can’t DEFUSE. It’s not to take a fight as FAST as possible, which is what you’re essentially doing. When you peek out backsite or push yellow and die you’re giving your life away for no reason. Think about it from the enemies’ perspective. If YOU are retaking, the GOLDEN scenario is that the enemy Jett gets greedy and peeks in the open for no reason and dies, giving you a free kill on your retake and making it way easier to defuse. The WORST scenario is if everyone is hiding and then you get hit with a sova dart or flash or something or you start fighting someone and then all of a sudden the enemy team swings off each others’ contact. Now in post plant as the attacker, make YOURSELF the worst-case scenario for the enemy. Don’t give them easy kills, make it annoying. Hide. Jiggle peek. Swing off your teammate. Swing off of recon. Ask for a flash. Ask your teammate to smoke you and play close inside of it. Be the post-plant defender you would HATE to play against.
